cases.head: 1e8d2e2f880cfe1d9bcbdfbc6078cb6b72fd35ce
cases.title: Add stream media source
cases.body:
<!--
 Hello, and thank you for your interest in contributing to the .NET MAUI Toolkit! 

 Before you submit please check that this work relates to one of the following:
 - Bug fix
    If you haven't yet opened an Issue that reports the bug in detail, provides a reproduction sample, and has been verified + reproduced by a member of the .NET MAUI Toolkit core team, please do that before submitting a Pull Request.
 - Feature/Proposal
    If you haven't yet submitted a Proposal that has been Championed by a .NET MAUI core team member, please instead open a Discussion at https://github.com/communitytoolkit/maui/discussions/new where we can discuss the pros/cons of the feature and its implementation. 
 Any PR submitted that does not fit with the above options will be closed.
 -->

 ### Description of Change ###

Adds StreamMediaSource support to MediaElement so media can be played directly from a .NET Stream.

This is intended for scenarios where media should remain in memory or within the app sandbox, rather than being written out to a file or fetched from an external URL. It enables workflows such as capturing or generating media in-memory and previewing it before persisting it.

The change adds a new MediaSource subtype and wires it through the existing MediaElement pipeline on supported platforms:
- Windows: uses WinMediaSource.CreateFromStream with IRandomAccessStream conversion
- Android: uses a custom ExoPlayer IDataSource implementation backed by Stream
- iOS/macOS: uses AVAssetResourceLoader to serve stream data to AVPlayer
- Tizen: explicitly reports stream playback as unsupported

The API follows the existing MediaSource patterns, including a MediaSource.FromStream(Stream) factory method and direct use of StreamMediaSource.

 <!-- Describe your changes here. This only needs to be brief as the linked issues below will already cover the detailed changes. -->

 ### Linked Issues ###
 <!-- Provide links to issues here (#35 will link to issue number 35). Ensure that a GitHub issue was created for your bug/proposal and it has been approved/Championed. -->

- Related discussion: https://github.com/CommunityToolkit/Maui/discussions/2968

 ### PR Checklist ###
 <!--
 Please check all the things you did here and double-check that you got it all, or state why you didn't do something.

 If anything is unclear please do ask :)
 -->
 - [x] Has a linked Issue, and the Issue has been `approved`(bug) or `Championed` (feature/proposal)
         **Note:** Has a linked discussion, not issue, however was discussed and approved by @TheCodeTraveler, @ne0rrmatrix and @VladislavAntonyuk  on the standup today (see: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gF1YSJyxAB8)
 - [x] Has tests (if omitted, state reason in description)
 - [x] Has samples (if omitted, state reason in description)
 - [x] Rebased on top of `main` at time of PR
 - [x] Changes adhere to [coding standard](https://github.com/CommunityToolkit/Maui/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code---best-practices)
 - [x] Documentation created or updated: https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/CommunityToolkit/pull/642


 ### Additional information ###

 <!-- 
 Please use this to aid the reviewer, this could include stating which platform(s) have been tested
 -->
 

- This work is currently linked to discussion 2968 rather than a formal issue.
- The feature proposal originated from secure-app scenarios where media must remain in-memory and within the app sandbox.
- Sample app updates are included to demonstrate stream-backed playback.
- Tizen is not supported at this stage and reports that limitation explicitly.
- Tested platforms: Windows, Android, iOS/macOS as applicable to the implementation.


## What Was Added

### Core Class
- **`StreamMediaSource.shared.cs`**: New `MediaSource` subclass that wraps a .NET `Stream`
  - Includes `Stream` bindable property
  - Implicit operators for convenient Stream conversion
  - Factory method `MediaSource.FromStream(Stream)`
  - Follows the same pattern as `FileMediaSource`, `UriMediaSource`, and `ResourceMediaSource`

### Platform-Specific Implementations

#### Windows (`MediaManager.windows.cs`)
- **Implementation**: Uses `WinMediaSource.CreateFromStream()` with `IRandomAccessStream`
- **Status**: ✅ Fully Supported
- **Method**: Leverages `WindowsRuntimeStreamExtensions.AsRandomAccessStream()` to convert .NET streams to Windows Runtime streams
- **Helper**: `StreamExtensions.windows.cs` - Provides `GetMimeType()` extension method

#### Android (`MediaManager.android.cs`)
- **Implementation**: Custom `StreamDataSource` implementing ExoPlayer's `IDataSource` interface
- **Status**: ✅ Fully Supported
- **Method**: Created custom data source that reads from .NET Stream and integrates with ExoPlayer's `ProgressiveMediaSource`
- **Helper**: `StreamDataSource.android.cs` - Contains `StreamDataSource` and `StreamDataSourceFactory` classes
- **Features**:
  - Supports seeking if stream is seekable
  - Handles range requests
  - Proper resource cleanup and disposal

#### iOS/macOS (`MediaManager.macios.cs`)
- **Implementation**: Uses `AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate` to provide custom data source
- **Status**: ✅ Fully Supported
- **Method**: Creates custom URL scheme (`stream://media`) and uses `AVAssetResourceLoader` to intercept loading requests
- **Helper**: `StreamAssetResourceLoader.macios.cs` - Custom delegate that feeds stream data to `AVPlayer`
- **Features**:
  - Works with both audio and video
  - Supports seeking if stream is seekable
  - Integrates seamlessly with existing `AVPlayer` architecture

#### Tizen (`MediaManager.tizen.cs`)
- **Status**: ❌ Not Supported
- **Reason**: Platform limitation - throws `NotSupportedException` with helpful message

## Usage Examples

```csharp
// Using factory method
MediaSource source = MediaSource.FromStream(myStream);

// Using implicit conversion
MediaSource source = myStream;

// Direct instantiation
var streamSource = new StreamMediaSource { Stream = myStream };

// Assigning to MediaElement
mediaElement.Source = MediaSource.FromStream(myStream);
```

## Files Modified

### New Files
1. `MediaSource/StreamMediaSource.shared.cs` - Core class
2. `Platforms/Android/StreamDataSource.android.cs` - Android implementation
3. `Views/StreamAssetResourceLoader.macios.cs` - iOS/macOS implementation
4. `Views/StreamExtensions.windows.cs` - Windows helper extensions

### Modified Files
1. `MediaSource/MediaSource.shared.cs` - Added `FromStream()` factory method
2. `Views/MediaManager.android.cs` - Added stream support via custom DataSource
3. `Views/MediaManager.windows.cs` - Added stream support via `CreateFromStream()`
4. `Views/MediaManager.macios.cs` - Added stream support via `AVAssetResourceLoader`
5. `Views/MediaManager.tizen.cs` - Added NotSupportedException for streams
6. `Converters/MediaSourceConverter.shared.cs` - Added `StreamMediaSource` case

## Technical Details

### Android Implementation
The Android implementation uses ExoPlayer's extensibility model:
- `StreamDataSource` implements `IDataSource` interface
- Reads data from .NET Stream on demand
- `StreamDataSourceFactory` creates instances for ExoPlayer
- Integrates with `ProgressiveMediaSource.Factory`

### iOS/macOS Implementation
The iOS/macOS implementation uses Apple's official extension mechanism:
- Creates `AVUrlAsset` with custom URL scheme
- `AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate` intercepts resource loading requests
- Provides stream data through `AVAssetResourceLoadingDataRequest`
- Supports both content information and data requests

### Windows Implementation
The Windows implementation uses built-in .NET stream conversion:
- Converts .NET Stream to `IRandomAccessStream` using `AsRandomAccessStream()`
- Uses `WinMediaSource.CreateFromStream()` API
- Provides default MIME type (can be enhanced for better type detection)

## Considerations

### Stream Lifecycle
- Streams are **not** automatically disposed by the MediaElement
- Callers are responsible for managing stream lifetime
- Consider keeping streams open for the duration of playback
- Seeking requires seekable streams

### MIME Type Detection
- Windows: Returns generic `"application/octet-stream"` by default
- iOS/macOS: Defaults to `"video/mp4"` assumption
- Future enhancement: Could detect MIME type from stream content (magic bytes)

### Performance
- Streams should support efficient random access for best performance
- Non-seekable streams may have limited functionality
- Consider buffering strategies for network streams

## Future Enhancements

1. **MIME Type Detection**: Implement magic byte detection to automatically determine content type
2. **Tizen Support**: Investigate if Tizen platform can support stream-based playback
3. **Stream Properties**: Add optional properties to `StreamMediaSource` for MIME type hint
4. **Buffering Options**: Add configurable buffering strategies for different stream types
5. **Progress Reporting**: Add stream read progress callbacks for monitoring

cases.head: c926adcf6e0be826e3313fc503a92b53a78f8ef8
cases.title: Fix SMP scheduler evicting task when preemption is disabled
cases.body:
## Summary

Fixes #1376 — SMP scheduler evicting a task that has preemption disabled via `vTaskPreemptionDisable()`.

In the SMP time-slicing path of `xTaskIncrementTick()`, `xYieldPendings[xCoreID]` was set to `pdTRUE` unconditionally without checking `xPreemptionDisable`. The later yield-processing block correctly skipped acting on it for preemption-disabled cores, but the **stale flag remained**. When a subsequent ISR (e.g. `xTaskGenericNotifyFromISR()`) called `prvYieldForTask()` — which correctly did not yield — it then checked `xYieldPendings[portGET_CORE_ID()]` and found the stale `pdTRUE`, erroneously setting `*pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken = pdTRUE`. This triggered `portYIELD_FROM_ISR()` → `vTaskSwitchContext()` → `prvSelectHighestPriorityTask()`, which evicted the preemption-disabled task.

## Changes (three-layer fix)

- **Root cause** (`xTaskIncrementTick`): Guard the time-slicing `xYieldPendings[]` assignment with a `configUSE_TASK_PREEMPTION_DISABLE` check so the flag is never set for cores running preemption-disabled tasks.

- **Defense in depth** (4 functions): In `xTaskResumeFromISR`, `xTaskRemoveFromEventList`, `xTaskGenericNotifyFromISR`, and `vTaskGenericNotifyGiveFromISR` — save `xYieldPendings[portGET_CORE_ID()]` before calling `prvYieldForTask()` and only report a yield if the flag transitioned from `pdFALSE` to `pdTRUE`. This eliminates false positives from any stale flags.

- **Safety net** (`vTaskSwitchContext` SMP path): Add a `xPreemptionDisable` check analogous to the existing `uxSchedulerSuspended` check. If a context switch is somehow triggered for a core whose task has preemption disabled, the switch is deferred (`xYieldPendings = pdTRUE`) and will execute when `vTaskPreemptionEnable()` calls `prvYieldCore()`.

## Configuration

Only affects SMP builds with:
```
configNUMBER_OF_CORES > 1
configUSE_TASK_PREEMPTION_DISABLE == 1
configUSE_PREEMPTION == 1
configUSE_TIME_SLICING == 1
```

Single-core builds are completely unaffected (all changes are inside `#if ( configNUMBER_OF_CORES > 1 )` or equivalent guards).

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify existing FreeRTOS SMP unit tests pass
- [ ] Test on dual-core SMP hardware (e.g. ESP32-S3) with preemption-disabled task + concurrent ISR notifications + same-priority time-slicing tasks (the scenario from #1376)
- [ ] Verify that preemption re-enablement (`vTaskPreemptionEnable`) still triggers deferred yields correctly
- [ ] Verify single-core builds are unaffected

cases.head: 2378227172859b977f576fa1a1e3dfd4b52fa524
cases.title: ci: fix grype-remediation-suggestions trigger, run ID resolution, underfixed false-positives, and least-privilege
cases.body:
Five correctness and security issues across the Grype automation workflows, including a condition that silently prevented the remediation-suggestions workflow from ever running automatically.

## `grype-remediation-suggestions.yml`

- **Drop `head_branch` guard** — `workflow_run.head_branch` reflects the branch owning the workflow file (`main`), not the branch checked out internally. The `== 'pre-update-release'` condition always evaluated false for scheduled runs.
- **Fix `workflow_dispatch` run ID fallback** — when `run_id` is omitted, `github.event.workflow_run.id` is empty on `workflow_dispatch` events. Now resolves via API: prefers the most recent successful `Weekly Grype Security Scan` run on `pre-update-release` within the last 7 days, falls back to the absolute latest if none found.
- **Filter PRs from issue search** — `issues.listForRepo` returns both issues and PRs; added `&& !i.pull_request` to prevent accidentally updating a PR body instead of the tracking issue.

## `dependabot-grype-guard.yml`

- **Drop `pull-requests: write`** — the workflow only writes to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and uploads artifacts; issue/PR creation from scan results is handled by `grype-remediation-suggestions.yml`. Only `contents: read` is required.
- **Scope `underfixed_updates` to High/Critical fixable vulns** — the previous logic false-positived when a package had an unrelated unfixable High vuln alongside a Medium fixable vuln. Added `fixed_high_critical_recommendations()` that filters to High/Critical severity before checking fix state; a package is only flagged underfixed if it was changed *and* still carries a fixable High/Critical finding in the PR image.

```python
# Before: any fixable vuln on the package triggered the check
underfixed_updates = [pkg for pkg in changed if pkg in recs and ("High" in severities or "Critical" in severities)]

# After: only packages with High/Critical fixable vulns are considered
high_critical_recs = fixed_high_critical_recommendations(pr)  # scoped to sev ∈ {High, Critical}
underfixed_updates = [pkg for pkg in changed if pkg in high_critical_recs]
```

cases.head: ac6e2196f5c307fd09fa6ad8a64ba9ada14ab385
cases.title: fix: verify wrapper-backed runtime binaries via direct exec
cases.body:
## What changed - replace the in-container manifest probe shell in `scripts/verify.sh` with per-entry verification driven by the checked-out runtime manifest - keep shell-based smoke checks for normal binaries - execute wrapper-backed binaries, currently `gemini`, via direct `docker exec ...args` so verify matches the direct-exec path that works in staging ## Why - staging deploy `24170400181` was healthy, but `verify.yml` run `24170520305` still failed on `failed_smoke:gemini:/opt/daisy/bin/gemini --version` - live staging proved the wrapper works when executed directly with `docker exec daisy-openclaw-gateway-1 /opt/daisy/bin/gemini --version` - the failing path was verifier shell mediation, not image provisioning ## Affected files - `scripts/verify.sh` ## Risks / blast radius - limited to runtime verification behavior - wrapper-backed entries now bypass the in-container shell during smoke checks; non-wrapper binaries still use the existing shell path ## Verification performed - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh` - `git diff --check` - live staging evidence: - `docker exec daisy-openclaw-gateway-1 /opt/daisy/bin/gemini --version` succeeds - prior `verify.yml` failure only occurred through the shell-probe path ## Remaining unverified - PR CI after this verifier-only change - post-merge staging verify rerun ## Deployment / rollback impact - requires normal merge -> Docker Release -> staging dry-run -> staging deploy -> verify sequence - rollback is the prior merged verifier behavior if this path regresses ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Chores** * Standardized and consolidated runtime-binary verification into reusable probe routines. * Detects target architecture reliably and selects repo-side runtime manifests accordingly. * Distinguishes wrapper vs non-wrapper binaries to perform appropriate existence and smoke checks, recording resolved paths. * Improved error handling and clearer diagnostics for missing or failing runtime checks.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the fix is well-scoped and matches the verified staging execution path. The core change is correct: replacing the shell-mediated probe with direct docker exec for wrapper-backed binaries matches the live staging evidence. All inputs are properly quoted via printf '%q', and the complexity guard prevents shell-metacharacter injection before any remote execution. The one comment left is a P2 duplication nit that does not affect correctness. Non-wrapper binaries are unchanged. No files require special attention.

Vulnerabilities

 No security concerns identified. User-controlled inputs (binary paths, smoke suffixes) are passed through `printf '%q'` quoting before being embedded in remote commands. The smoke-suffix complexity guard explicitly rejects shell metacharacters (`'`, `"`, `\`, `|`, `>`, `<`, `;`, `&`) before any remote execution. Credentials and host paths are validated against allow-list patterns before use.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | scripts/verify.sh | Core verification script refactored to use direct docker exec for wrapper-backed binaries; logic is sound with minor code-duplication between the container and image branches of build_target_direct_exec_command. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[verify_runtime_binaries_for_target] --> B[Check manifest exists in target] B --> C[Detect target arch via dpkg] C --> D[Load manifest entries for arch from repo] D --> E{For each entry} E --> F{wrapper_type == node-entrypoint?} F -- Yes --> G[build_target_wrapper_test_command\ncheck -x binary_path] G --> H[gce_ssh: test -x /opt/daisy/bin/binary] H --> I[build_target_direct_exec_command] I -- container --> J[sudo docker exec container binary args] I -- image --> K[sudo docker run --rm --entrypoint binary image args] J --> L[gce_ssh smoke: output discarded] K --> L L --> M[append_runtime_bin_line binary binary_path] F -- No --> N[Build shell probe\ncommand -v + smoke_command] N --> O[gce_ssh: sh -c probe] O --> P[append_runtime_bin_line binary resolved_path] M --> E P --> E E --> Q[printf runtime_bins] ```

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. `scripts/verify.sh`, line 444-447 ([link](https://github.com/hughdidit/daisy-agency/blob/1b1dee6d1bac6a4716673e79f2e871d72effcee1/scripts/verify.sh#L444-L447)) **Unbound variable `runtime_binary_probe_escaped` breaks sandbox smoke check** `runtime_binary_probe_escaped` is referenced here but is never assigned anywhere in the script. Under `set -euo pipefail`, the `-u` flag causes bash to abort with a "parameter not set" error the moment this line is reached — so Check 8 will hard-fail (not just return a bad exit code) whenever `sandbox_enabled == "true"`. The old Check 3 logic appears to have built a probe script and stored it in this variable, which the sandbox check then reused. This PR switched Check 3 to per-entry iteration from the repo manifest (lines 177-214) but left this reference intact without providing a replacement probe for the sandbox image. The sandbox image (`docker run --rm ...`) can't use the same per-entry `docker exec` path, so it needs its own solution — for example re-using the non-wrapper shell probe loop or a purpose-built probe command for the sandbox image.
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: scripts/verify.sh Line: 186-208 Comment: **Duplicated smoke-suffix logic in `image` branch** The `image` branch of `build_target_direct_exec_command` (lines 186–208) reproduces the same smoke-suffix extraction, complexity guard, and argument-splitting logic that already lives in `build_direct_exec_smoke_command`. The `container` branch avoids the duplication by calling `build_direct_exec_smoke_command`, but the `image` branch does not. If the guard conditions or arg-splitting rules ever change, they would need to be updated in both places. Consider refactoring the `image` branch to reuse `build_direct_exec_smoke_command` as well, passing a suitable `command_prefix`: ```bash image) command_prefix="sudo docker run --rm --entrypoint $(printf '%q' "${binary_path}") ${target_escaped}" build_direct_exec_smoke_command "${command_prefix}" "${binary_path}" "${binary}" "${smoke_command}" ;; ``` Note: `build_direct_exec_smoke_command` already strips the binary prefix and re-quotes each arg, so it produces a correctly-formed command string for both modes. How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````

cases.body:
Contributors currently have no standardized local dev environment — setup requires manually installing Python 3.11, `uv`, and configuring tooling. This adds a Dev Container so the environment is reproducible and ready to code in one click.

## What's added

### `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`
- `python:3.11-slim` base (consistent with production `Dockerfile`)
- Installs `git`, `curl`, `build-essential`, and `uv`
- Non-root `vscode` user (UID/GID 1000)

### `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`
- `postCreateCommand` runs `uv venv && uv pip install -e '.[dev]'` automatically on container creation
- Port `8811` forwarded (OpenAPI proxy)
- Python interpreter pre-pointed at the `uv`-managed `.venv`
- VS Code extensions: `ms-python.python`, `ms-python.vscode-pylance`, `ms-python.black-formatter`, `charliermarsh.ruff`, `eamodio.gitlens`, `mhutchie.git-graph`, `redhat.vscode-yaml`, `ms-azuretools.vscode-docker`

cases.title: Aktivitetspenger inntektsrapportering
cases.body:
This pull request introduces support for "inntektsrapportering" (income reporting) for the "Aktivitetspenger" benefit throughout the codebase. It adds new Kafka topics, extends enums and services, and implements new API endpoints and data models to handle income reporting submissions, including integration with the task management system.

The most important changes are:

**Kafka Topics and Configuration**
* Added three new Kafka topics for handling different stages of "aktivitetspenger-inntektsrapportering" (`mottatt`, `preprosessert`, `cleanup`) in `aktivitetspenger-inntektsrapportering-topics.yml`, with appropriate ACLs and retention policies.
* Registered the new topic in `Topics.kt` and updated the topic selection logic to handle the new `AKTIVITETSPENGER_INNTEKTSRAPPORTERING` type. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-81c50ef5bed7712d8e2e6dbe22dd4503af3ab806c70c1d0181b21efab9cad3b2R38) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-81c50ef5bed7712d8e2e6dbe22dd4503af3ab806c70c1d0181b21efab9cad3b2R62)

**Domain Model and API**
* Introduced `AktivitetspengerInntektsrapportering` and `AktivitetspengerInntektsrapporteringInnsending` data classes to represent and process income reporting submissions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4e656c3718b45418384544295f09723b186c40f7b987e71b0ff43c8e733b4db2R1-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c64c0a0381387e10349d506f520be966d0071b378b7835f62a17fd725d7680eaR1-R76)
* Added a new POST endpoint `/inntektsrapportering/innsending` in `AktivitetspengerController` to receive income reporting submissions.

**Service Layer and Integration**
* Implemented the `inntektrapportering` method in `AktivitetspengerService` to handle submissions: validates, registers, sends metrics, and marks related tasks as completed using `UngBrukerdialogApiService`.
* Integrated with the task management system to fetch task periods and mark tasks as solved after income reporting is received. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-21a79806cca2803fba2a7999a021f690656e4623a2be288e1e651d4a18f714c9R35) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-21a79806cca2803fba2a7999a021f690656e4623a2be288e1e651d4a18f714c9R76-R121)

**Enums and Supporting Structures**
* Extended `Ytelse`, `YtelseType`, and `KafkaStreamName` enums to support the new income reporting flow for Aktivitetspenger, including mapping topics to the new type. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dbe2ba52d0c42fe8e7f07082cd545c62e2b498177e0b7268ee16f2b13378415cR67) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-dbe2ba52d0c42fe8e7f07082cd545c62e2b498177e0b7268ee16f2b13378415cR92) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-eac334b6458b0e89981131a5806709b194ae23b3f970d3dce8ab2315787a9513L187-R194) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-5fbf2360f35cacd01444cd957c7ed98d25c44513834cc9555c1d5664d3e281ccR121-R125) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-1b714cf039c2fdec162bc757b2b540d606a799a8e4448e4eb33491d05eafa710R29)
* Updated PDF generator logic to handle the new reporting type.

These changes establish the full technical foundation for receiving, processing, and tracking "inntektsrapportering" for Aktivitetspenger in the system.

cases.head: 343e5688641d1d989d8535e0276a08a1adc9ede8
cases.title: Add support for MCP Catalogs from private repos and non-github repos
cases.body:
## Summary

Addresses #6341 #5543

Adds support for pulling MCP catalogs from private git repositories, and generalizes catalog source URL support beyond GitHub to any HTTPS git host.

### Credential storage
- Admins can supply a Personal Access Token (PAT) when adding a git source URL via the UI
- Tokens are stored securely in the GPTScript credential store (keyed by catalog UID + URL hash), never in the resource spec
- The API returns `"*"` as a presence indicator — the actual token is never exposed

### Git platform support
- **GitHub**: supported with or without `.git` suffix; falls back to `GITHUB_AUTH_TOKEN` env var for default catalog if no per-URL token is configured
- **GitLab**: supported with or without `.git` suffix; supports subgroups (`group/subgroup/repo.git`)
- **Self-hosted**: supported with `.git` suffix (e.g. `https://git.example.com/org/repo.git`)

### Repository size limits
- **GitHub**: pre-clone size check via GitHub API (fast, no bandwidth wasted)
- **GitLab**: pre-clone size check via GitLab projects API when a token is available (`read_api` scope required, but 403 error is ignored)
- **All other hosts**: clone is monitored in real time with a custom FS

### Other changes
- Context is propagated from the controller sync request through all HTTP calls and the git clone
- URL with `.git` suffix is handled correctly (stripped before constructing clone URL and API calls)
- Tooltip in the UI explains supported URL formats
- Enable editing in the UI. Most code for it existed already

## Testing guide
- [x] Add a public GitHub repo as a source URL — verify sync works
- [x] Add a private GitHub repo with a PAT — verify sync works and token is not visible in the UI after saving
- [x] Add a private GitLab repo (`https://gitlab.com/org/repo.git`) with a PAT — verify sync works
- [x] Add a GitLab repo with subgroups (`https://gitlab.com/group/subgroup/repo.git`) — verify sync works
- [x] Add a URL with `.git` suffix — verify it works the same as without
- [x] Remove a source URL that has a stored token — verify the credential is cleaned up
- [x] Verify `GITHUB_AUTH_TOKEN` env var still works as a fallback for GitHub default catalog when no per-URL token is set
- [x] Attempt to clone large repository that isn't on Github or Gitlab (`https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git`)

cases.head: 4db0ddeaea75e5d1d1a312473465153ed8f60661
cases.title: feat(migration-toolkit): add import-users command with chunked Partial Import
cases.body:
## Summary

Adds the `keycloak-migrate import-users` subcommand to the migration toolkit, closing #490.

## What this does

- Reads `users.json` produced by `keycloak-migrate transform`
- Two credential resolution modes:
  - **Cluster mode** (default): reads admin username/password from the Kubernetes secret generated by the operator (`{name}-admin-credentials`), verifies the Keycloak instance is `Ready` before importing
  - **Explicit flags** (`--username`/`--password`): for environments where RBAC doesn't permit secret reads
- Uses Keycloak's Partial Import API (`POST /admin/realms/{realm}/partialImport`) with chunked batching (default 500 users/batch) to stay within HTTP body limits
- **SKIP mode by default** — idempotent, re-running is safe even if users already exist
- Token lifecycle management with automatic refresh 30 s before expiry
- Hard fail on `errors > 0` in any batch response (non-atomic batches won't be rolled back automatically)
- File age check (default 24 h) to prevent importing stale exports
- `--dry-run` flag to preview without making API calls

## Tests

- 8 loader tests covering valid array, empty array, JSON object rejection, missing username field, invalid JSON, max age enforcement, max age skip, and file not found
- 7 chunk() unit tests covering empty, single user, exact batch size, batch+1, multiple batches, and batch larger than input

## Documentation

- `docs/how-to/migration-toolkit.md`: full `import-users` command reference section
- `docs/how-to/export-realms.md`: new "Option B: Automated Import" pointing to the command, with manual Partial Import bumped to Option C

## ADR

Decision record `093-user-import-via-migration-toolkit.yaml` documents the design rationale: why SKIP not FAIL, why cluster credentials by default, and why this is a one-time migration tool rather than a continuous sync.

## Testing checklist

- [x] `task toolkit:test` — all pass
- [x] `task test:all` — all pass (quality + unit + integration)
